Supplement

/SUH-pluh-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Supplement means something added to complete a thing or to make up for a deficiency.

The doctor recommended a vitamin D supplement to make up for the long, sunless winters.

Worked Example

Her part-time tutoring served as a supplement to the family's income during the slow season.

The tutoring money doesn't replace the family's income — it's an extra amount added on to make up for a shortfall. Adding something extra to cover a lack is exactly what a supplement is.

How Supplement Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

addition

addition: something joined to what already exists

add-on

add-on: an extra piece attached to the main thing

boost

boost: an added amount that strengthens or helps

Antonyms

reduction

reduction: an amount taken away or cut

cutback

cutback: a deliberate decrease, especially in spending or supply

How Strong Is It? — top-up → supplement → replacement

top-up vs. supplement

top-up vs. supplement: A top-up adds a little more of what you already have; a supplement fills a genuine gap.

replacement vs. supplement

replacement vs. supplement: A supplement supports the main thing; a replacement pushes it aside entirely.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — sup-

Prefix — sup-: up from below (a form of sub-)

Root — ple-

Root — ple-: to fill (Latin plere)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Sup- (up from below) + ple- (to fill) + -ment (result): something that fills a shortage from underneath — an extra piece supplied to make up for what's lacking.

Use the root in a new word: deplete

Use the root in a new word: deplete: Weeks of drought began to deplete the town's reservoir.

Root Check

Word Choice

Everyday & academic

A supplement adds something extra to make up for a lack — a vitamin supplement, a supplement to your income, a supplemental report. Don't blur it with complement (which completes or perfects a specific pairing rather than topping up a shortage) or with implement (which is about carrying out a plan, not adding anything). Supplement also works as a verb: 'She supplements her salary with weekend shifts.'
